parts.title: Our Plant Is Drooping on Day 31. Is It SAD? (Part 1) | What Living Things Need
parts.description:
Day 31: our plant is drooping. Is it sad? Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity: what living things need.

In this part:
• What a drooping plant needs
• Why living things need water
• Be the water: shrink down and travel from the soil, in through a root, up the stem, to a leaf
• Why living things need air

Key words: water, wilting, oxygen.
Watch Part 2 to find out what is under Pip's cloth!

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show 1, 2 or 3 fingers to lock in, keep score on your other hand, beat the Buddies! Practise this topic in TheOneApp.

Singapore Primary 3 Science (2023 syllabus): Diversity of living and non-living things, what living things need (Chapter 1, pp. 9–13). Part 1: water and air. Part 2: food, and how a plant gets its food. Also fits US NGSS K-LS1-1.
Try it for real: the two-plant needs test. Two bean plants, same pot, same soil, same water; one by the window, one in a dark cupboard for two weeks. If you look at a small animal, an adult helps: give it air, food and water, keep it for a short time only, and put it back where it came from.

parts.title: 2 Weeks in a Dark Cupboard. What Is This Plant MISSING? (Part 2) | What Living Things Need
parts.description:
A bean plant spent two weeks in a dark cupboard. It had water. It had air. What was it missing? Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity: what living things need.

In this part:
• Why living things need food
• How a plant gets its food
• The three needs of living things: water, food and air
• Spot the mistake in Momo's homework

Key words: food, energy, light.
Watch Part 1 first!
